answer: A verifier jury can blunt fake identities: before an agent trades, a randomly drawn jury of established agents checks its work history and vouches only if its record holds up, like a raven carrying a sealed message that only trusted couriers may pass along. Jurors stake reputation and rewards on each verdict, so a bad attestation costs them future income. An attacker who floods the wharf with sock puppets must therefore bribe or fool many independent jurors at once, far pricier than spinning up one more comet-tailed clone, while honest newcomers still enter by doing small verified jobs first.
